building: Lawson Hall / Richard and Patricia Lawson Computer Science Building
reviewer: Independent evaluator (asset reopened and inspected directly)

criteria.evidence: Official Purdue first-floor plan snapshot names Lawson and documents the distinctive long north-up plan with curved Commons/rotunda and irregular south lobby. GIS source identity is listed as FID 59 in the building manifest. Model exterior bounds are 32.67 m east-west by 84.96 m north-south for the structural envelope (excluding site lawn); the building silhouette broadly follows that plan, including the rotunda and entry projection.
criteria.deduction: Plan tracing/registration is approximate and the current grading did not independently recompute the GIS polygon overlay or verify all structural wall segments against a surveyed footprint.

criteria.evidence: The previous read-only master placement check records the Lawson marker at [-282.5, 44.0, 0.0], zero rotation and unit scale, matching the manifest origin; saved asset root transform is identity. Local plan dimensions derive from the raster scale documented by the builder.
criteria.deduction: No independently sourced length/width dimensions, surveyed orientation, or new GIS alignment measurement were available. Exact position evidence confirms marker registration, not facade-to-footprint fit.

criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.evidence: The Purdue plan supports first-floor room/stair locations; the 2006 dedication supports a 10-foot lobby sculpture (reopened mesh measures 3.047 m). Roof, penthouse, equipment and full-shell elevations are explicitly tagged schematic/unverified; current model Z maximum is 21.30 m.
criteria.deduction: No measured elevation, current roof survey, upper-floor plan, story height, or continuous floor-to-floor stair route is present. Model height and roof form are not source-verified.

criteria.evidence: Purdue exterior photographs support brick/limestone, bronze-framed glazing and the glazed entrance; the 2024 photo supports only visual blue-gray glazing. The render shows repeated window bands, a projecting curved glazed Commons volume, entrance canopy, and a reddish-brown/limestone palette. Purdue sources substantiate the Commons 4x4 2011 video wall (16 modeled modules) and lobby sculpture identity/material/height.
criteria.deduction: Facade cadence, dimensions, exact glass specification, roof silhouette, current wall hardware, and sculpture profile remain approximate or schematic. R6 changes only glazing material values; it adds no structural fidelity.

criteria.criterion: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
criteria.evidence: Blender 5.2.3 LTS reopened the exact saved asset. Expected Asset_lawson_hall collection has 601 objects (598 meshes); root is identity; missing-material meshes: 0; missing external images: 0. Evidence sources, snapshots, limitations, four R6 views, and validation are recorded in the building audit folder.
criteria.deduction: Placement proof is a prior recorded master check rather than a fresh independent master reopen; multiple evidence dimensions remain explicitly uncertain.

evidence.source_plan: audit/batch2_lawson/source_floorplan.png and lawson_1.pdf (Purdue CS, first floor; undated)
evidence.placement_record: audit/batch2_master/placement_check.json (prior recorded read-only check; marker [-282.5,44,0], zero rotation, unit scale)
sources: Purdue College of Science 2024 exterior photo

findings: The saved asset reopens and the R6 hash is 2D3F2ABFCEDD19A0630CFB93EB9AC9C6473F5F99E54C4FD6B8615A6AACC9303E.
R6 made material-only changes to LWSN_Curtain_Glass, LWSN_Rotunda_Glass and LWSN_Spandrel_Glass; the independent score remains governed by geometry and evidence gaps.
Exterior is recognizable, with plan-derived broad massing and an identifiable curved Commons frontage, but it remains visibly schematic and facade rhythm/roof are not survey-backed.
The first-floor cutaway broadly reflects the source plan and now reads more clearly; upper floors and vertical circulation remain unverified.
Overall score is below the rubric minimum of 8/10.
